data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The structural bias of mod 6 over 2^31 states is mechanistically too small (~0.67 extra counts per face per 10M draws for the favored faces) to push any face count outside 2 standard deviations at n=10000, so the generator will be fair by the stated criterion.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the simulation returns counts where any face falls outside [10000/6 - 2*sigma, 10000/6 + 2*sigma], this conjecture is refuted.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the LCG's period is much shorter than 2^31 (e.g., if the multiplier does not produce a full period), the bias analysis based on uniform state coverage would be invalid.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the initial transient (first 10000 terms from X_0=42) happens to concentrate on a biased subset of residues, the structural-bias argument may not predict the actual counts.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Bias quantification: 2^31 = 2147483648 = 6 * 357913941 + 2, so residues 0 and 1 each occur 357913942 times per full cycle, residues 2-5 each occur 357913941 times. Per 6*357913941 = 2147483646 draws, faces 1-2 get one extra occurrence each (bias ~4.67e-7 per draw). At n=10000, the expected excess for faces 1-2 over faces 3-6 is ~4.67e-3 counts \u2014 utterly negligible compared to the 2-sigma tolerance of ~105 counts. The affine LCG with full-period multiplier visits every state in its cycle exactly once before repeating, so at n=10000 (far short of the full period ~2^31), the sequence is a deterministic walk through a tiny prefix of the cycle. The structural bias is too small to matter, but only the simulation can confirm the actual counts fall within tolerance.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
